title.value: Predicting Adverse Radiation Effects in Brain Tumors After Stereotactic Radiotherapy With Deep Learning and Handcrafted Radiomics
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus of the research on predicting adverse radiation effects in brain tumors using Deep Learning and radiomics.
title.quote: Keek SA, Beuque M, Primakov S, Woodruff HC, Chatterjee A, van Timmeren JE, Vallières M, Hendriks LEL, Kraft J, Andratschke N, Braunstein SE, Morin O and Lambin P (2022) Predicting adverse radiation effects in brain tumors after stereotactic radiotherapy with deep learning and Handcrafted Radiomics. Front. Oncol. 12:920393.

extractions.description: The study investigates the potential of machine learning models built on radiomics features, deep learning (DL) features, and patient characteristics to predict adverse radiation effects (ARE) in patients with brain metastases (BM) after stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT). The models aim to identify high-risk patients, potentially aiding clinical decision-making by informing patients of their ARE risk and considering alternative therapies.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on medical research specifically related to predicting adverse radiation effects in brain tumor treatments, which does not align directly with climate or ecological sustainable development goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Machine learning models built on radiomics features and DL features extracted from BM combined with patient characteristics show potential to predict ARE at the patient and lesion levels. These models could be used in clinical decision making, informing patients on their risk of ARE and allowing physicians to opt for different therapies.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on predicting medical adverse effects using deep learning, which does not relate to climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: Machine learning models built on radiomics features and DL features extracted from BM combined with patient characteristics show potential to predict ARE at the patient and lesion levels.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no additional secondary categories that the paper could be classified under within the realm of climate or ecological sustainable development as it is strictly focused on medical applications.
secondary_categories.quote: Patients with BM treated with SRT are at risk of developing ARE, such as RN. Early identification of these patients can help in clinical decision making.

primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-categories related to climate or ecological sustainable development do not cover the medical predictive modeling scope presented in the paper.
primary_sub_category.quote: The DL model predictions and the radiomics-based model predictions per lesion agreed for 32% of the external dataset.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No relevant secondary sub-categories within climate or ecological sustainable development are applicable due to the medical nature of the research.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Lastly, for ARE (and, to a lesser degree, TP), treatment is one of the primary factors. In this study, multiple-dose-treatment-related variables have been included.

applications.justification: The applications discussed in the paper are centered around improving clinical decision-making in oncology treatment, not applicable to climate or ecological sustainable development.
applications.quote: These models could potentially be used to aid clinical decision making for patients with BM treated with either gamma knife or EBRT.

new_primary_category.justification: The study focuses on applying deep learning for predictive imaging and modeling in a medical context, specifically to improve oncology outcomes.
new_primary_category.quote: Radiomics is able to predict lesions at a high risk of ARE, especially when combined with DL features.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper specifically discusses the optimization of stereotactic radiotherapy in oncology using advanced imaging and prediction techniques.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We hypothesize that models trained with radiomics features, DL features, and patient characteristics or a combination thereof can predict the occurrence of ARE in patients with BM, both lesion specific and patient specific.
